name: a defined code with no arm stops being refused, so a new rc is swallowed as #202 was
expect: a defined code with NO arm and NO row is refused (rc 4, row removed)

name: two rc tuples stop being a cannot-run, so the guard picks one and guesses
expect: TWO rc tuples is a cannot-run — the guard must not pick one and guess

name: handled_codes ignores the code set it is given, so a narrowed probe answers over everything
edits: return {rc for rc in sorted(codes) if observe(hook_src, rc, _PROBE)}
return {rc for rc in sorted({0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}) if observe(hook_src, rc, _PROBE)}
expect: handled_codes honours a NARROWER code set — the parameter is read, not assumed

name: silence is reported as output, so a code the hook DROPS counts as handled — #202's whole shape
expect: a silent code is NOT handled — #202 was a code the hook received and dropped

name: the hook's non-zero exit is accepted instead of refused — a fail-open at the seam
expect: a hook that exits non-zero is a cannot-run

name: output that is not the documented envelope is treated as silence rather than a cannot-run
expect: a hook that prints something other than its envelope is a cannot-run

name: the dead-arm probe range goes back to 15, so a reachable arm above it passes as clean — round 5 H1
edits: def dead_arms(hook_src: str, defined: set[int], probe_max: int = 255)
def dead_arms(hook_src: str, defined: set[int], probe_max: int = 15)
expect: a dead arm at 16 is caught — round 5 H1, the old window stopped at 15

name: the probe range stops including probe_max, so the top of the range is unguarded
edits: codes = [rc for rc in range(probe_max + 1) if rc not in defined]
codes = [rc for rc in range(probe_max) if rc not in defined]
expect: the probe range INCLUDES probe_max itself

name: R1's wiring is cut: the call site passes every defined code as handled (anchored on the rule's own assignment: four entries cannot share one)
expect: R1 is WIRED — the missing 0) arm reaches the verdict

name: R2's wiring is cut: dead_arms still RUNS and its result is discarded — round 5 H2
expect: R2 is WIRED — dead_arms' result is still READ at the call site (round 5 H2)

name: the raw TARGET count stops being compared, so a target the reader drops lets the names bind to the wrong numbers — round 5 M3
expect: a target the reader drops is refused even when the VALUES line up

name: the DISTINCT-value count stops being compared, so two codes may share a value and the set arithmetic absorbs it — round 5 L4
expect: two codes sharing a value are refused — round 5 L4

name: only a MISSING file is a refusal, so an unreadable one exits 1 with a traceback again — round 5 M2
expect: a path that exists and cannot be read is CannotRun, never a pass

name: the dead-arm cap never fires, so a forwarding catch-all arrives as hundreds of lines naming the wrong cause — round 5 L1
expect: many dead arms collapse to ONE problem naming the catch-all — round 5 L1

name: a bash FATAL ERROR is read as silence again, so R1 and R2 cannot tell a crashing arm from a quiet one — round 7 H2
expect: a hook that writes to STDERR is a cannot-run, never silence — round 7 H2
